title: Visual metacognition — system must know when its own visual evidence is unreliable
description: IABV must detect when its own visual capture is unreliable (black image, offscreen window, low information, partial occlusion, wrong window, low resolution) and NOT treat it as valid evidence. This is a metacognition capability: the system observes its own observation and classifies it.
resume_hint: All 6 detection scenarios now implemented: offscreen/minimized, blank capture, user/IABV browser mismatch, partial occlusion, wrong window captured, resolution too low. OSES findings detect repeated patterns.
next_action: Verify on live Windows that new visual metacognition detections fire correctly during external consultation captures.

metadata.covered_by_pr: P0.3 visual alignment slice + P0.4 shared reality

real_failure_case.root_cause: ControlCenterViewModel accepted offscreen/minimized window as valid target and captured black image as evidence
real_failure_case.user_reaction: a mí sí me funciona y a él no

metadata.p03_fix: _window_rect_is_captureable() rejects rect with left/top <= -30000. _capture_is_low_information() rejects blank_probability >= 0.90. _validate_visual_evidence_result() sets status=visual_unresolved instead of visual_captured. Runtime audit traces visual_evidence_snapshot with status=unresolved.
metadata.p04_fix: _build_shared_reality_handoff() creates causal package. _detect_user_mismatch_claim() identifies user's 'it works for me' signals. _build_causal_explanation() produces 'Tu vista vs Vista de IABV' comparison. This is metacognition applied to the user/system perception gap: the system knows it cannot see what the user sees and explains why.
metadata.p05_fix: OSES _shared_reality_handoff_findings() converts repeated visual mismatches into structured findings with evidence, frequency, last case, and recommended action. PortableContext exports compact summary. The metacognition loop is now: detect invalid capture → explain to user → learn from repetition → prioritize fix.
